speaker: Unknown
en: So we're here in Mountain View today with PG himself at the original offices doing your talk that you do for the YC batch.
zh: 所以我们今天在山景城，和 PG 本人在最初的办公室里，你正在给这一批 YC 学员做你常做的那场演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I looked it up.
zh: 我查了一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is actually the 47th YC batch.
zh: 这实际上是第 47 批 YC。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I've been trying to calculate that number and I wasn't sure exactly what it was.
zh: 你知道，我一直在试着计算那个数字，但我不太确定具体是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: No wonder I'm not too worried about this talk.
zh: 难怪我对这场演讲不太担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've done it that many times.
zh: 我已经讲了那么多次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It changes a little bit.
zh: 它会有一些变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the 21st year also of YC.
zh: 这也是 YC 的第 21 个年头。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the weird thing is I make the talk from scratch every time.
zh: 你知道，奇怪的是，我每次都是从头开始写这篇演讲稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I probably say the same things over and over, but I always feel like I should, like, I think, oh, my God, you know, think a couple hours beforehand.
zh: 我可能一遍又一遍地说着同样的东西，但我总觉得我应该——比如说，我想：哦天哪，我得提前几个小时想一想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oops, I better, I'm just talking to YC.
zh: 糟糕，我还是要和 YC 的人谈话的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I better think in advance a little bit about what to say.
zh: 我最好提前想一点要说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I open up a text file and start typing things.
zh: 所以我打开一个文本文件，开始打字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how it always is.
zh: 一直都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any tidbits from today that are new from winter?
zh: 那今天有没有什么和冬季那批相比是新的内容？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, most of the things, most of starting a startup here, this is an actually interesting point.
zh: 没有，大部分东西，大部分创业的内容——这其实是个有意思的点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of starting a startup is the same.
zh: 创业的大部分东西都是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of starting a startup is always the same, right?
zh: 创业的大部分东西从来都是一样的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: In, you know, microprocessors or AI or like the internal combustion engine, it's always the same stuff.
zh: 无论是微处理器、AI 还是内燃机，一直都是同样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, in that case, let's run through some questions.
zh: 那么，那样的话，我们来过一些问题吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you recently posted that the startups YC funds now are much more serious than they were in the supposedly good old days.
zh: 所以你最近发帖说，YC 现在投资的初创公司比所谓的美好旧时光里的要严肃得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you mean by that?
zh: 你这话是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what I meant by supposedly good old days is people are always saying that YC has jumped the shark, you know?
zh: 嗯，我说的「所谓的美好旧时光」是指，人们总是在说 YC 已经江河日下了，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, I remember when people started saying this, which is in about like 2008, right?
zh: 而且我记得人们开始这么说的时候，大概是 2008 年左右，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: YC is always this thing that was great, but now it's not what it was, right?
zh: YC 永远是那种「曾经很了不起，但现在不如从前」的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they can't say it was always terrible.
zh: 因为他们不能说它一直都很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to admit it was once great.
zh: 他们必须承认它曾经很了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if they want to attack it, they have to say it's fallen, right?
zh: 所以如果他们想攻击它，就必须说它衰落了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was good, but now it's not.
zh: 它曾经很好，但现在不行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always been, it's always not good anymore.
zh: 它一直都是——它一直都不再好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what I meant by the supposedly good old days, because the old days are what people claim used to be good.
zh: 所以这就是我说的「所谓的美好旧时光」的意思，因为旧时光就是人们声称过去曾经很好的那段时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like in the old days, there was a lot of things like Reddit, right?
zh: 但就像旧时光里也有很多像 Reddit 这样的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which valuable as it is, is not exactly intercontinental ballistic cargo, right?
zh: 它虽然有价值，但算不上洲际弹道货物，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I did office hours with recently.
zh: 我最近还和它们做了办公时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about that for an idea?
zh: 这个点子怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's like an ICBM, except instead of exploding, it lands.
zh: 就像一枚洲际弹道导弹，只不过它不爆炸，而是降落。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's ambitious.
zh: 很有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And drops stuff off.
zh: 而且还把东西卸下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's serious, right?
zh: 是啊，这就很严肃，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get much more serious than an intercontinental ballistic cargo.
zh: 没有比洲际弹道货物更严肃的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What were some of the other serious ones?
zh: 还有其他哪些严肃的例子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, curing cancer.
zh: 嗯，治愈癌症。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a startup in this batch.
zh: 这一批里就有一家初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's all sorts of different approaches to curing cancer.
zh: 我是说，有各种各样不同的治愈癌症的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say fund many of them because like anyone working would be good.
zh: 我说资助他们中的许多个,因为不管哪个能做成都是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like one way to approach curing cancer is vaccines.
zh: 比如治疗癌症的一种思路是疫苗。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one end, right?
zh: 那是一端,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The opposite end is therapies, right?
zh: 另一端是疗法,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a startup in this batch that is...
zh: 所以这一批里有一家初创公司……

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically doing on-demand research for people with cancer, you know?
zh: 基本上是在为癌症患者做按需研究,你懂的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I like about it is they're sort of inflicting on cancer the death of a thousand cuts, which may be the way to defeat it because, you know, it's notoriously not the sort of thing where you just like come up with a cure for cancer.
zh: 我喜欢它的地方在于,他们是在对癌症施加“千刀万剐”,这可能正是击败它的方式,因为你知道,癌症向来不是那种你能一下子发明出治愈方法的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, maybe you do if these vaccines work.
zh: 我是说,如果这些疫苗管用,也许真能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you do, right?
zh: 也许真能做到,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or maybe the way you fight it is the death of a thousand cuts.
zh: 又或者,对抗它的方式就是千刀万剐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're actually really interesting because they helped another YC group.
zh: 而且他们真的很有意思,因为他们帮助过另一家 YC 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, right.
zh: 是啊,对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's part of the whole YC community.
zh: 这就是整个 YC 社区的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They helped Sid from GitLab deal with his cancer, which he has done very successfully.
zh: 他们帮助 GitLab 的 Sid 对抗他的癌症,而且他做得非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, he approached it like a startup, right?
zh: 我是说,他把这件事当成一家初创公司来对待,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And these were essentially his co-founders in that de facto startup.
zh: 而在那家事实上的初创公司里,他们基本上就是他的联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's funny because I remember thinking after that, you know,
zh: 有意思的是,我记得那之后我在想,你懂的,

speaker: Unknown
en: I always had this process going of what would be a good startup idea, right?
zh: 我脑子里一直有一个关于什么是好的创业点子的思考过程,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember after that saying, you know, somebody should start a startup to do for everyone what Sid did for himself.
zh: 我记得那之后我说过,应该有人创办一家初创公司,把 Sid 为自己做的事做给所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, not only is this startup happening, it's the people who actually did it for Sid.
zh: 而现在,不仅这家初创公司真的出现了,而且做它的人正是当年真正帮 Sid 做成这件事的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it couldn't be better.
zh: 所以再好不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was so delighted when I realized that one was happening.
zh: 当我意识到这件事正在发生的时候,我简直太高兴了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I think his essay that I went founder mode on my cancers.
zh: 是啊,而且我记得他写过一篇文章,叫“我以创始人模式对待我的癌症们”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's a very good way of describing what he did.
zh: 是啊,这个说法很好地描述了他做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, using another YC term to attack his cancer.
zh: 是啊,用另一个 YC 术语来攻击他的癌症。

speaker: Unknown
en: So along that vein, I was rereading the essay you wrote in 2012, where you coined the term frighteningly ambitious.
zh: 顺着这个思路,我在重读你 2012 年写的那篇文章,你在里面创造了“惊悚级野心”这个说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Frighteningly ambitious ideas.
zh: 惊悚级野心的点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of those ideas have actually gotten done since then.
zh: 那些点子里其实有很多在那之后已经实现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like which ones?
zh: 比如哪些?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, a new Google, that was one of them, right?
zh: 嗯,一个新的 Google,那就是其中一个,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out, look, I sort of predicted this, right?
zh: 结果你看,我算是预测到了这一点,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That the way you make a new Google is not by attacking them head on.
zh: 做出一个新的 Google 的方式,不是正面硬刚它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to wait for things to change so much that their model is obsolete.
zh: 你得等到情况变化大到他们的模型已经过时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's when you can do it.
zh: 那时候你才做得成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what OpenAI is, right?
zh: OpenAI 就是这么回事,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I realized very early on, like, after using OpenAI, like, whoa, I don't use Google anymore.
zh: 比如,我很早就意识到了,用了 OpenAI 之后,哇,我不再用 Google 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't use searches.
zh: 我不再用搜索了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I really wanted from searches was not web pages.
zh: 我真正想从搜索里得到的不是网页。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted information.
zh: 我想要的是信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not just ask the AI for the information, right?
zh: 为什么不直接问 AI 要信息呢,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure everyone's now had this experience.
zh: 我确信现在每个人都有过这种体验了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was incubated at YC.
zh: 而且它是在 YC 孵化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊,对对对。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of Sam's many side projects.
zh: Sam 众多副业项目之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so along the same veins of around ambitious as a term, I am curious when you figured out why a founder needs to be not just unusually talented in technical ability or something else, but they actually have to be really ambitious as well.
zh: 所以顺着“野心”这个词的脉络,我很好奇你是什么时候想明白,为什么创始人不仅要在技术能力或其他方面异于常人地有才华,而且他们还必须真的非常有野心。

speaker: Unknown
en: When did I figure out that founders had to be really ambitious?
zh: 我是什么时候想明白创始人必须非常有野心的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I already knew that before we started YC because when we started YC, we already had all this experience of doing a startup ourselves, right?
zh: 我觉得在创办 YC 之前我就已经知道了,因为我们创办 YC 的时候,我们已经有了自己亲身做初创公司的全部经历,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we knew that it was grueling.
zh: 所以我们知道那是极其煎熬的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need something to drive you through all those obstacles.
zh: 而你需要某种东西驱使你穿过所有那些障碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, being dutiful is not enough.
zh: 说实话，仅尽本分是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The obstacles are too fearsome for mere dutifulness to do it.
zh: 障碍太可怕了，仅凭尽本分做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's got to be something driving you, and you call it ambition.
zh: 所以必须有某种东西在驱动你，你称之为雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of ambition, I assume, is wanting to be a billionaire someday.
zh: 我猜雄心的一部分，是希望有一天成为亿万富翁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you'd be surprised, actually.
zh: 嗯，实际上你会感到惊讶的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me more.
zh: 多说一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what actually motivates founders day to day?
zh: 你知道创始人每天真正被什么驱动吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The fear of failure.
zh: 对失败的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even though they're doing this thing that if they succeed, they'll be super rich, that does motivate them.
zh: 尽管他们在做这件事，如果成功了就会超级有钱，这确实会激励他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the thing that motivates them.
zh: 但真正驱动他们的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: At any given moment is the fear of disaster, looking like a fool, the server crashing, right?
zh: 在任何时刻，都是对灾难的恐惧，怕看起来像个傻瓜，怕服务器崩溃，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you're running some online service and your server's crashing, you're not thinking, I gotta deal with this because if I deal with it, I'll become a billionaire.
zh: 比如你在运营某个在线服务，你的服务器正在崩溃，你不会想，我得处理这个，因为处理好了我就会成为亿万富翁。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're thinking,
zh: 你在想的是，

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh no, the server is crashing.
zh: 哦不，服务器正在崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be a disaster.
zh: 这将是一场灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: The engine of my model train set is falling off the edge of the table.
zh: 我的模型火车头的引擎要从桌子边缘掉下去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to go and save it.
zh: 我得赶过去救它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you're thinking at any given time.
zh: 这就是你在任何时刻所想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't want your model train set to break.
zh: 你只是不想让你的模型火车坏掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You put your head down and work on the model train set for 10 years, and then you lift your head up and like, holy shit.
zh: 你低头埋头在模型火车上干十年，然后抬起头，我的天。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I add up the value of all my shares at the last round valuation, I'm a billionaire.
zh: 如果我按上一轮估值把所有股份加起来，我是个亿万富翁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it takes people by surprise when it happens.
zh: 但当它发生时，人们会感到意外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's great.
zh: 是的，太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I'm the first to tell them.
zh: 有时候我是第一个告诉他们的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I do the math.
zh: 比如我会算一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, wait, according to your last round, you're a billionaire.
zh: 我说，等等，按你上一轮的估值，你是个亿万富翁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, oh, yeah, I am.
zh: 然后他们说，哦，是啊，我是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the way we want it.
zh: 这正是我们想要的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious, can you tell me a story about a founder where when they started YC, they were maybe not ambitious enough, and then they became very ambitious during the batch?
zh: 我很好奇，你能不能讲一个创始人的故事：他们在加入 YC 时可能雄心不够，然后在批次期间变得非常有雄心？

speaker: Unknown
en: Those stories are rare because most of this quality is inborn.
zh: 这样的故事很少见，因为这种特质大多是天生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Sam Altman famously was extremely formidable the first time I met him before we even accepted him.
zh: 比如 Sam Altman，我第一次见他时就极其厉害，那时我们甚至还没录取他。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's more the rule than the exception.
zh: 而且这更多是常态而非例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the one case where you see founders
zh: 所以你能看到创始人的那一种情况是——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that they lack ambition.
zh: 并不是他们缺乏雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more like they've been trained not to show it.
zh: 更像是他们被训练得不表现出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when you're young, you're often in situations where you're supposed to be obedient.
zh: 因为当你年轻的时候，你常常处于那种你应该服从的处境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not supposed to go off and do what you want.
zh: 你不应该跑去做自己想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're supposed to do what people tell you.
zh: 你应该做别人告诉你去做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you have pushy parents who tell you to do what they want, right?
zh: 也许你有强势的父母，让你去做他们想要的事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you've never let yourself go.
zh: 所以你从来没让自己放开过。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the one case.
zh: 这就是那一种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even then, I would argue that the person was ambitious.
zh: 但即便如此，我会说这个人是有雄心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd just been trained not to show it.
zh: 他们只是被训练得不表现出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, that's a good point because I think nowadays a lot of people think about startups like another badge that they should collect along their resume.
zh: 实际上，这是个好观点，因为我觉得现在很多人把创业想成履历上应该收集的又一个徽章。

speaker: Unknown
en: Only if it fails.
zh: 只有失败的时候才是徽章。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it works, it's like your life's work.
zh: 如果成功了，那就是你毕生的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have any more badges, right?
zh: 你就不再需要任何徽章了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what kind of badge is a failed startup?
zh: 那么，一家失败的创业公司算什么徽章呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not much of a badge.
zh: 算不上什么徽章。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if people think that, they're not thinking it through, right?
zh: 我认为如果人们这么想，那他们是没想清楚，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like honestly, we would get...
zh: 说实话，我们会……

speaker: Unknown
en: It was quite early on in YC's history when people started applying to YC for the prestige, right?
zh: 在 YC 历史相当早期的时候，人们开始为了声望而申请 YC,对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they would apply to Harvard hoping they would get in.
zh: 就像他们申请哈佛，希望自己能被录取。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the thing is, if you apply to Harvard and get in, you should do it because no matter how stupid you are, there's easy majors you can choose and sort of slide through.
zh: 但问题是，如果你申请哈佛并被录取了，你应该去，因为不管你多笨，总有一些容易的专业可以选择，然后混过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll get a Harvard degree and everybody will be impressed with you.
zh: 你会拿到哈佛学位，所有人都会对你印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: With startups, there's no easy major, right?
zh: 而创业公司没有容易的专业，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like applying to Harvard and being forced to study theoretical physics.
zh: 这就像申请了哈佛，却被强制去学理论物理。

en: It's really rough if you're not very hardworking and clever and determined.
zh: 如果你不是很勤奋、聪明和坚定的话，那会非常艰难。

en: And so these people trying to do YC as a credential.
zh: 所以这些想拿 YC 当作资历的人，

speaker: Unknown
en: They had no idea what they were asking for.
zh: 他们完全不知道自己在要求什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't realize, like, this is not, this is a really, really unsuitable credential.
zh: 他们没意识到，这不是，这是一个非常、非常不合适的资历。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many easier ways to get credentials.
zh: 有很多更容易获得资历的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to seem cool, like starting a startup is just about the least efficient way to do it.
zh: 如果你想显得酷，创业差不多是效率最低的方式。

zh: 它残酷地艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you won't seem cool for years, years of brutal hardness before anyone will think you're cool.
zh: 而且你好多年都不会显得酷，要经过多年残酷的艰难，才会有人觉得你酷。

speaker: Unknown
zh: 百分之百。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you were describing some of the founders before you used the word formidable, can you tell us a little bit more about how that word came to be, what it means to you as well?
zh: 你之前描述一些创始人时用了「 formidable 」这个词，能多讲讲这个词是怎么来的吗？以及它对你意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, a lot of the language of Y Combinator is Maya and Jessica's private language, right?
zh: 嗯，Y Combinator 的很多语言都是 Maya 和 Jessica 的私人语言，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we already had this word before we started YC, like for a certain kind of person.
zh: 所以在我们创办 YC 之前，我们就有这个词了，用来形容某一类人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I described it in an essay.
zh: 我在一篇文章里描述过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, I think that it's someone who gets what they want.
zh: 我说，我认为这种人就是能得到自己想要的东西的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the test, right?
zh: 这就是检验标准，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you get what you want?
zh: 你能得到你想要的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because how formidable are you if you don't get what you want, right?
zh: 因为如果你得不到你想要的，那你有多厉害呢，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's someone who gets what they want in any situation.
zh: 所以这是一个在任何情况下都能得到自己想要的东西的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you invest in them and you have stock in their company and they have stock in this company, your interests are aligned, if they get what they want, you get what you want.
zh: 所以如果你投资他们，你在他们公司持有股份，他们也持有公司的股份，你们的利益就是一致的——如果他们得到了他们想要的，你就得到了你想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why investors want people who are formidable.
zh: 这就是为什么投资人想要厉害的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty good.
zh: 说得挺好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because they get a part of what the founder gets.
zh: 是啊，因为他们能分到创始人所得的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So changing tracks a little bit, at startup school, Patrick Collison recently said that lean startups may be dead.
zh: 那么稍微换个话题，在 Startup School 上，Patrick Collison 最近说精益创业可能已经死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did he?
zh: 他这么说了？

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of that is because he says, you know, it's really easy to raise money these days.
zh: 他这么说的一部分理由是，你知道，现在融资真的很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI lets you work on many things in parallel.
zh: AI 让你能并行做很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could, you know, spin out a bunch of agents and work on a bunch of things.
zh: 你可以，你知道，派出一堆智能体，同时做一堆事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with him or would you have a rebuttal?
zh: 你同意他吗，还是你会反驳？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never really been clear what a lean startup is.
zh: 我一直不太清楚精益创业是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we already had a kind of startup that we funded in YC, and maybe it has a lot of overlap with what was described in this book, the lean startup, but I haven't actually read it.
zh: 我是说，我们在 YC 已经投资过一种创业公司，它可能和这本书《精益创业》里描述的有很大重叠，但我其实没读过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I mean, why would I, right?
zh: 所以，我是说，我为什么要读呢，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Tolkien didn't read all those other fantasy books people wrote.
zh: 托尔金可没去读别人写的那些其他奇幻小说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't exactly know what a lean startup is, but if you tell me what qualities you might think might be obsolete, maybe I could answer that.
zh: 所以我并不确切知道精益创业是什么，但如果你告诉我你认为哪些特质可能过时了，也许我可以回答那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say starting with just a little bit of money on a very focused area.
zh: 比如说，从只有一点点钱、在一个非常专注的领域开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mean it might be dead starting with a little bit of money?
zh: 你的意思是，从一点点钱开始这件事可能已经死了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot of things you can do for cheap.
zh: 我觉得有很多事情可以低成本做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, tokens are very expensive at the moment, but that's just because there's a shortage of GPUs.
zh: 我是说，目前 token 非常昂贵，但那只是因为 GPU 短缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Token prices will...
zh: Token 的价格会……

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly inference prices at any given level of inference go down dramatically, like 30x a year or something like that.
zh: 在任何给定的推理水平上，推理的价格肯定会大幅下降，大概一年降 30 倍之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even token prices are somewhat misleading because you're getting higher quality tokens over time.
zh: 所以即使是 token 价格也有点误导性，因为随着时间推移，你得到的是更高质量的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think, no, technology always gets cheaper.
zh: 所以我认为,不,技术总是会变得更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can still start a startup on not much money.
zh: 我认为你仍然可以用不多的钱创办一家初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if it's a rocket startup or any of these?
zh: 即使是火箭初创公司,或者这类公司?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's harder to start a rocket startup on no money.
zh: 没什么钱要创办火箭初创公司会更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even a rocket startup, you can start on not much money because what you do is you adjust for how much money you've got.
zh: 但即使是火箭初创公司,你也可以用不多的钱起步,因为你要做的是根据你有多少钱来调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't build an actual rocket.
zh: 你造不出真正的火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you can build is you can build a design for a rocket and show that to, and you can simulate it, right?
zh: 你能造的是一个火箭的设计方案,然后把它展示给——而且你可以做仿真,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or show it to experts.
zh: 或者展示给专家看。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's convincing enough, you can go to investors and get a bit of money to do the next stage.
zh: 如果它足够有说服力,你就可以去找投资人,拿到一点钱去做下一个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're always able to raise another round, right?
zh: 你总是能够再融一轮,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So you just do what you can on the money you got.
zh: 所以你就在你拿到的钱的基础上,做你能做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: As long as you can get to some kind of milestone, then you can convince investors to give you more.
zh: 只要你能达到某种里程碑,你就能说服投资人给你更多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think Philip from StarCloud was saying that they basically just wrote a white paper and booked a launch, and they raised the money for StarCloud.
zh: 是啊,我记得 StarCloud 的 Philip 说过,他们基本上就是写了一份白皮书,预订了一次发射,然后就为 StarCloud 融到了钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, nothing as convincing as booking a launch, right?
zh: 是啊,没有什么比预订一次发射更有说服力的了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got to happen if you've booked a launch.
zh: 如果你预订了发射,那这事就必须发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he's a huge famous expert.
zh: 但他是位非常有名的权威专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the stuff he works on, right?
zh: 在他所研究的领域,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So he comes with automatic cred.
zh: 所以他自带天然的信誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier for him to do that than some kid who just graduated from college.
zh: 对他来说,做这件事比一个刚大学毕业的孩子要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's transition to talk a little bit about AI more broadly.
zh: 那么让我们转个话题,更宽泛地聊一聊 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what surprised you about AI.
zh: 我很好奇 AI 有什么让你惊讶的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was studying AI back in the 1980s, a very different kind of AI that would never have worked.
zh: 我在上世纪 80 年代研究过 AI,那是一种完全不同、永远不可能成功的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it was a joke.
zh: 我是说,那简直就是个笑话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been thinking about this a lot.
zh: 所以我一直在思考这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I spent a lot of time thinking about what AI would eventually be like.
zh: 我花了很多时间思考 AI 最终会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way we thought it was all going to play out was you start out with
zh: 而我们当时设想的发展路径是从

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a perfect fly, right?
zh: 比如一只完美的苍蝇开始,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what?
zh: 你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't do much.
zh: 它做不了多少事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a fly, like a fly's brain, right?
zh: 它就像一只苍蝇,就像苍蝇的大脑,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It can only do what a fly does, but it does it as well as a fly, right?
zh: 它只能做苍蝇能做的事,但它做得和苍蝇一样好,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you work your way up from flies to mice, you know, to cats, and eventually you get monkeys and then humans, right?
zh: 然后你从苍蝇往上做,到老鼠,你知道,到猫,最终做到猴子,再到人类,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But at every point, you're perfect.
zh: 但在每一个阶段,你都是完美的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're doing what they do well.
zh: 你把它们能做的事做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead, what we got was basically
zh: 结果相反,我们得到的基本上是

speaker: Unknown
en: A full-on human but full of shit, right?
zh: 一个完完全全的人类,但满嘴胡扯,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the first AIs, the first versions of ChatGPT were like an undergrad trying to bullshit his way through a paper.
zh: 比如最早的 AI,ChatGPT 的最初版本,就像一个本科生在论文里硬着头皮胡编乱造。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something plausible sounding, full human stuff, like not even this fly stuff, full human but like terrible, right?
zh: 听起来像模像样,完全是人类层面的东西,而不是那种苍蝇级别的东西,完全是人类水平但烂得很,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you start, and so instead of starting with perfect and then working your way up to human, you start with human and then work your way towards perfect.
zh: 所以你是这样起步的——不是从完美开始然后逐步做到人类水平,而是从人类水平开始,然后逐步走向完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's sort of the opposite, the opposite quality ended up.
zh: 所以有点相反,最终被优化的是相反的品质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ended up being the one that got optimized.
zh: 最终被优化的是那一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody expected that.
zh: 没有人预料到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody expected when the first plausible AI turned up, it would be like a bullshitting undergraduate, right?
zh: 没有人预料到,当第一个像模像样的 AI 出现时,它会是一个胡编乱造的本科生,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a slot machine.
zh: 就是一台老虎机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and it still has a lot of that flavor, doesn't it?
zh: 是啊,而且它至今仍有那种味道,不是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hear all these stories about how AI is solving famous open problems in math, and I can't even get it to answer questions about when restaurants are open.
zh: 我听过所有这些故事,说 AI 在解决著名的数学开放难题,可我甚至没法让它回答关于餐馆什么时候营业的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what's called the jagged frontier.
zh: 这就是所谓的“锯齿状边界”(jagged frontier)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They must know things I don't know, or they have research versions.
zh: 它们一定知道一些我不知道的东西，或者它们有研究版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they can find out when restaurants are open.
zh: 也许它们能查到餐馆什么时候开门。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing, you are famously very good at taking complex topics and making them sound very simple.
zh: 另外一件事，你以擅长把复杂话题讲得非常简单而闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is the official PG definition of AGI?
zh: 那么，PG 对 AGI 的官方定义是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, well, honestly, I mean, could you do better than the Turing test?
zh: 哦，说实话，我是说，你能比图灵测试做得更好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The Turing, I think Turing was pretty good, right?
zh: 图灵，我觉得图灵已经相当不错了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the reasons, one of the ways I knew we were getting close to AGI was I actually had to go and look up the definition of the Turing test.
zh: 我知道我们接近 AGI 的原因之一，就是我居然得去查一下图灵测试的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: That in itself is a piece of evidence.
zh: 这本身就是一条证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what was the Turing test again?
zh: 就是，图灵测试又是什么来着？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we there already?
zh: 我们是不是已经到了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's happened now is we thought
zh: 我觉得现在的情况是，我们曾经以为

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in the day that AI would be sort of like this finish line and AGI would be this finish line.
zh: 在过去，AI 会像是这样一条终点线，AGI 会是这条终点线。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd cross it, it would be very clear.
zh: 我们会跨过它，一切会非常清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you're standing on the finish line, you realize it has width.
zh: 但当你站在终点线上时，你发现它是有宽度的。

speaker: Unknown
en: From back in the 1980s, it looks like it's just a line going across the horizon.
zh: 从 1980 年代回头看，它看起来只是一条横跨地平线的线。

speaker: Unknown
en: But here you realize, okay, some bits of AI are way across the finish line.
zh: 但到了这里你才意识到，好吧，AI 的一些部分已经远远跨过了终点线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some bits are like maybe in the middle of it.
zh: 有些部分大概在线的中间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knew the line had dimension?
zh: 谁知道这条线是有维度的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The finish line is actually this sort of smear.
zh: 终点线其实是一道模糊的 smear。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the best answer you can give is like, we're on the smear.
zh: 而我觉得你能给出的最好回答就是，我们在这道 smear 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out to be a smear and we're on it.
zh: 它原来是一道 smear，而我们就在上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why you can't get your restaurant times.
zh: 这也是为什么你查不到餐馆营业时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because they're in a bad part of the smear.
zh: 是啊，因为它们处于 smear 比较差的那一段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas the Ryman hypothesis, maybe we're already there.
zh: 而 Ryman 假设呢，也许我们已经到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, changing back to talk about startups.
zh: 好，换回聊聊创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the other thing you've said is that the best predictor of success for a startup is the pace that they ship new stuff.
zh: 你还说过的另一件事是，创业公司成功与否最好的预测指标是他们发布新东西的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: With AI, does that change?
zh: 在 AI 时代，这一点会变吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think there's a new metric?
zh: 你觉得会有新的指标吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, there's, I mean, we have all these powerful AI tools and there's still a lot of startups in this batch that are not shipping fast enough.
zh: 不会，不会，我是说，我们有了这么多强大的 AI 工具，但这一批里仍然有很多创业公司发布得不够快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so obviously there's variation in shipping speed.
zh: 所以显然发布速度是存在差异的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just the rate at which you can breeze things, you have to think of these ideas first, right?
zh: 这不仅仅是你能多快地发布东西的速度，你还得先想出这些点子，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone always asks me like,
zh: 大家总是问我，

speaker: Unknown
en: With all this AI, is anything still the same?
zh: 有了这一切 AI，还有什么是不变的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer is, so far, almost everything is exactly the same.
zh: 答案是，到目前为止，几乎所有事情都一模一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only weird new thing is that companies have these giant AI bills.
zh: 唯一奇怪的新东西是公司有了巨额的 AI 账单。

speaker: Unknown
en: It used to be startups' big cost was salaries.
zh: 以前创业公司最大的成本是工资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was all that mattered, salaries, right?
zh: 只有工资才重要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything else was cheap by comparison, because it was just laptops and people.
zh: 其他一切相比之下都便宜，因为不过就是笔记本电脑和人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, suddenly, you've got to pay for GPUs, you know?
zh: 而现在，突然之间，你得为 GPU 付费了，你知道吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Giant, giant.
zh: 巨大，巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, tens of thousands of dollars a day in tokens.
zh: 我是说，每天在 token 上花掉数万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm also curious, how does being in a batch like YC give founders an advantage?
zh: 我也很好奇，加入像 YC 这样的批次能给创始人带来什么优势？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of reasons.
zh: 原因有很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is starting a startup is normally a very lonely business.
zh: 一是创办创业公司通常是一件非常孤独的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have all this upside.
zh: 你有巨大的上行空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have complete control over what you're doing.
zh: 你对自己在做的事情拥有完全的控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: The downside is you don't have any colleagues.
zh: 缺点是你没有任何同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is like working in an office with all these colleagues, except you're all working on your own startups.
zh: 而这里就像是和所有这些同事一起在办公室工作，只不过你们各自都在做自己的创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's that.
zh: 就是这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have colleagues.
zh: 你有同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also learn from what the other startups are doing at the same time you are.
zh: 你还可以在创业的同时，向其他创业公司学习他们在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have some technical problem.
zh: 比如你遇到某个技术问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably somebody in the batch had that problem.
zh: 批次里很可能有人遇到过这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just ask them how they solved it, right?
zh: 你可以直接问他们是怎么解决的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And another advantage is what we call the YC GDP.
zh: 另一个优势是我们所说的 YC GDP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is, you have some sort of product, you can sell it to the startups in your batch.
zh: 就是，你有了某个产品，可以把它卖给你批次里的创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost no matter what it is, you can find some.
zh: 几乎不管它是什么，你总能找到一些买家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're the exact kind of users you want.
zh: 而且他们正是你想要的那种用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early adopters who decide quickly, right?
zh: 决策迅速的早期采用者，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they sort of have to at least listen to your pitch.
zh: 而且他们多少至少得听你推销一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you come up with the idea for YC?
zh: 你是怎么想出 YC 这个点子的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Gradually.
zh: 逐渐形成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Initially, the idea was just going to be we didn't have the batch idea at first.
zh: 起初，这个点子只是——我们一开始并没有批次这个概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: The part we had at first was to be an angel firm, because at that point, there were VC firms who would do these giant late stage rounds, and there were angel investors who were individual people.
zh: 我们最初有的想法是做一家天使投资公司，因为在那个时候，有一些风投公司会做这些巨额的后期轮次融资，也有一些天使投资人，是个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Investing their own money, but there were no angel firms.
zh: 投自己的钱，但没有天使投资公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the original idea, to be an angel firm, like a VC firm, but invest small amounts of money earlier and use standardized paperwork.
zh: 那就是最初的想法，做一家天使投资公司，像风投公司一样，但更早期投入小额资金，并使用标准化的文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, having decided that, we thought, all right, we need to learn how to be investors since we don't know how to be investors.
zh: 然后，在决定这么做之后，我们想，好吧，我们需要学习怎么当投资人，因为我们不知道怎么当投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll just fund a whole bunch of startups all at once.
zh: 那我们就一次性资助一大批创业公司吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought to ourselves, well, all these college students get summer jobs working at Microsoft.
zh: 于是我们心想，这些大学生都在微软做暑期工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wouldn't they like to start startups instead?
zh: 他们难道不想去创业吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll create this alternative to getting a summer job.
zh: 我们就来创建一个代替暑期工作的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why the batch takes place during the summer.
zh: 这就是为什么批次安排在夏天进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out to be the perfect length, but that was just an accident.
zh: 结果证明这是完美的时长，但那只是个意外。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought, we'll fund a whole bunch of startups.
zh: 于是我们想，我们要资助一大批创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll replace summer jobs.
zh: 我们将取代暑期工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be for current undergrads.
zh: 它是面向在读本科生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They won't mind if we're not real investors because they're not real founders, right?
zh: 他们不会介意我们不是真正的投资人，因为他们也不是真正的创始人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a bunch of college students.
zh: 只是一群大学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turned out in the course of that, we became real investors and they became real founders very quickly.
zh: 结果在这个过程中，我们很快变成了真正的投资人，他们也很快变成了真正的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this batch thing was so great.
zh: 而这个批次模式太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This thing that we just discovered by accident, we thought, all right, we're going to always do investing that way.
zh: 这个我们纯属偶然发现的东西，我们想，好吧，我们要一直用这种方式做投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: How has YC changed or not changed since it's grown?
zh: YC 在发展壮大之后有什么变化，或者没什么变化？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's changed very little.
zh: 变化很小。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically like the same thing, but more of it.
zh: 基本上还是同一件事，只是规模更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like the problems the startups have are pretty much the same.
zh: 你知道，创业公司遇到的问题基本都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot more of them, but they, you know, they live in small groups that are just like individual bits of YC.
zh: 数量多了很多，但是，你知道，他们以小组的形式存在，就像一个个小小的 YC。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things people saying, when people say YC is jump the shark, one of the things they always say is, oh, it's so big now.
zh: 所以，当人们说 YC 已经盛极而衰时，他们总会说的一件事就是，哦，现在规模太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, people used to say that back when we had 40 startups in the batch.
zh: 嗯，早在我们一个批次只有 40 家创业公司的时候，人们就那么说了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would say, oh, come on.
zh: 他们会说，哦，拜托。

speaker: Unknown
en: The old days are gone.
zh: 好日子一去不返了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's 40 startups in the batch, right?
zh: 一个批次有 40 家创业公司了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: People are always saying that.
zh: 人们总是在那么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you divide YC up into little bits where each startup is part of a pot of 70 startups, then it's just like they were back in 2012 when there were 70 startups.
zh: 而如果你把 YC 划分成小块，每家创业公司都属于一个 70 家创业公司的小组，那就和 2012 年有 70 家创业公司时一模一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you think the next trillion-dollar company comes from?
zh: 你认为下一家万亿美元公司会来自哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the founders of it like?
zh: 它的创始人是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The founders of it are formidable.
zh: 它的创始人是很厉害的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, that is the answer to your question.
zh: 事实上，那就是你问题的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to your question of where the next giant company comes from is it comes from the right founders, right?
zh: 下一家巨头公司来自哪里这个问题的答案是：它来自对的创始人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not some particular idea.
zh: 这不是某个特定的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it probably is some idea rather than others.
zh: 我是说，它可能确实是某种想法，而不是别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably not dog walking, right?
zh: 大概不会是遛狗吧，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe.
zh: 也可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows?
zh: 谁知道呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe.
zh: 也许吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe.
zh: 也许吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, startups' ideas are very mutable.
zh: 我是说，创业公司的想法是非常多变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it comes from the next trillion-dollar founders is where it comes from.
zh: 但它来自下一批万亿美元公司的创始人，这就是它的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they probably have good ideas.
zh: 而他们很可能有好想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever they're working on is probably promising.
zh: 无论他们在做什么，那件事很可能是有前景的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the founders in the future are going to look very different from the ones in the past?
zh: 你认为未来的创始人会和过去的看起来很不一样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to be robots.
zh: 他们会是机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope not.
zh: 我希望不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, no.
zh: 不，不，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founders, they still, I mean, we now have 20 years of data.
zh: 创始人，他们仍然，我是说，我们现在有 20 年的数据了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They still look exactly like they used to 20 years ago.
zh: 他们看起来仍然和 20 年前一模一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why should they change 20 years from now?
zh: 为什么 20 年后就应该变呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
